title: Broadcom plunges even as Q2 results, guidance top Wall Street's forecast (AVGO:NASDAQ)
author: Sigma Capital
metaDescription: Broadcom's shares fell 14.5% despite beating Q2 estimates and raising guidance, as investors were disappointed by flat AI revenue forecasts and below-consensus
excerpt: Broadcom's shares fell 14.5% despite beating Q2 estimates and raising guidance, as investors were disappointed by flat AI revenue forecasts and below-consensus Q3 guidance. The broader semiconductor sector also declined amid high bond yields.

content.introduction: Broadcom's shares fell 14.5% despite beating Q2 estimates and raising guidance, as investors were disappointed by flat AI revenue forecasts and below-consensus Q3 guidance. The broader semiconductor sector also declined amid high bond yields.
body: Broadcom declined alongside a broader semiconductor sector pullback, with investors rotating cautiously ahead of Nvidia's highly anticipated earnings Wednesday and as surging bond yields — the 30-year Treasury hitting a near-20-year high above 5.19% — pressured high-multiple tech stocks. Broadcom surged to near its 52-week high, driven by a major analyst upgrade from Wells Fargo, which raised its price target to $545 from $430 — one of the most dramatic large-cap semiconductor revisions of the year — arguing that AI semiconductor revenue is tracking 30–40% above prior Wall Street expectations. Despite the macro headwinds, Citi raised its price target on Broadcom to $500 (from $475), reiterating a Buy rating ahead of the June 3 fiscal Q2 earnings report, citing AI demand strength and Broadcom's $73B AI backlog anchored by long-term deals with Meta, Google, and Anthropic.

BREAKING: Broadcom (AVGO) shares plunge more than 14% in pre-market, erasing over $310 billion in market value following the company's fiscal Q2 earnings report. While the company technically beat top and bottom-line estimates, it disappointed high market expectations by:. • Keeping its fiscal year AI revenue forecast flat at $100 billion instead of raising it. • Issuing below-consensus FQ3 AI semiconductor revenue guidance ($16 billion vs. the $17.2 billion Wall Street expected). Shares of AI chip winners, including Marvell (MRVL), Nvidia (NVDA), and AMD (AMD), fell in premarket trading after Broadcom did not raise its AI semiconductor sales forecast for 2026.
